paragraphs.title: The Psalm Heading

easy.explanation: The verse begins, “How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD?”
easy.q: Who does the speaker address in verse 1?

easy.explanation: The speaker asks, “How long wilt thou forget me?”
easy.q: What does the speaker ask whether the LORD will do?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “how long wilt thou hide thy face from me?”
easy.q: What does the LORD hide from the speaker?

answers: Being forgotten and having God's face hidden
medium.explanation: The speaker asks how long the LORD will forget him and hide His face.
medium.q: What two concerns are repeated in verse 1?

answers: The speaker's question about the duration
medium.explanation: “For ever” intensifies the speaker's concern about how long the suffering will last.
medium.q: What does the phrase “for ever” emphasize?

medium.explanation: “Hide” means to keep from being seen.
medium.q: Which word in the verse means to conceal from view?

answers: He feels the trouble has continued too long
challenge.explanation: The repeated question conveys prolonged distress and impatience for relief.
challenge.q: What does the repeated “how long” suggest about the speaker's condition?

challenge.explanation: It is a sorrowful question directed to the LORD.
challenge.q: What kind of statement is “How long wilt thou forget me”?

challenge.explanation: Singing about salvation appears later, in verse 6, not in verse 1.
challenge.q: Which idea is not stated in verse 1?

paragraphs.idea: The heading identifies the text as a psalm for the chief musician and a psalm of David.

paragraphs.paragraph: The speaker feels that God has forgotten him and hidden His face from him. He faces the continuing need to find ways to escape, unending sorrow, and an enemy who is gaining power over him.
paragraphs.title: A Sense of Abandonment and Inner Distress

easy.explanation: He says, “How long shall I take counsel in my soul?”
easy.q: What does the speaker take in his soul?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “having sorrow in my heart daily.”
easy.q: What is in his heart daily?

easy.explanation: The speaker asks how long his enemy will be exalted over him.
easy.q: Who is exalted over the speaker?

answers: He is trying to deal with his trouble
medium.explanation: Taking counsel suggests that he is searching inwardly for a way through his distress.
medium.q: Why does the speaker take counsel in his soul?

medium.explanation: The KJV says that he has sorrow in his heart “daily.”
medium.q: How often does the speaker experience sorrow?

answers: Raised above and gaining power over him
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the enemy as prevailing or gaining advantage.
medium.q: What does “exalted over me” mean in this context?

answers: The continuing nature of the distress
challenge.explanation: The repeated question stresses that the suffering has lasted for a long time.
challenge.q: What does the repetition of “how long” emphasize in verses 2–3?

answers: Sorrow in my heart and mine enemy exalted over me
My heart rejoices and I sing
I have trusted in thy mercy
challenge.explanation: The first phrase describes inward sorrow, while the second describes external opposition.
challenge.q: Which phrase describes the speaker's inner and outer troubles together?

answers: Both his inner life and circumstances are troubled
Both show that he has already been rescued
challenge.explanation: His daily sorrow and the enemy's strength show distress within and around him.
challenge.q: How do the speaker's sorrow and the enemy's power intensify his sense of abandonment?

paragraphs.idea: The speaker feels that God has forgotten him and hidden His face from him. He faces the continuing need to find ways to escape, unending sorrow, and an enemy who is gaining power over him.

paragraphs.paragraph: The speaker asks God to answer him and enlighten his eyes so that he will not fall into the sleep of death. He asks that his enemy and foes not be allowed to rejoice in his defeat and downfall.
paragraphs.title: A Plea for Salvation and Rescue from Defeat

easy.explanation: He says, “Consider and hear me, O LORD my God.”
easy.q: What does the speaker ask the LORD to do?
What does the speaker ask God to lighten?

easy.explanation: He says, “lest I sleep the sleep of death.”
easy.q: What does the speaker fear sleeping?

answers: So that he may receive help and guidance
So that his enemy may rejoice
So that he can hide his face
medium.explanation: Lightened eyes suggest renewed life, understanding, and help in the crisis.
medium.q: Why does the speaker ask God to lighten his eyes?

answers: I have trusted in thy mercy
I will sing unto the LORD
medium.explanation: He asks for rescue so his enemy cannot claim victory.
medium.q: What does the speaker want to prevent his enemy from saying?

medium.explanation: The phrase is a poetic description of dying.
medium.q: What does “the sleep of death” mean in context?

answers: Both ask God for active help
challenge.explanation: The speaker asks God to respond and provide the light and strength needed for rescue.
challenge.q: How are the requests to be heard and to have one's eyes lightened related?

answers: His enemies rejoicing over his defeat
challenge.explanation: He does not want his enemy to say he has prevailed or his foes to rejoice when he is moved.
challenge.q: What outcome does the speaker want to prevent?

answers: From distress to an urgent plea for help
challenge.explanation: The speaker turns his distress into direct requests for God's answer, light, and protection.
challenge.q: What movement occurs in these verses?

paragraphs.idea: The speaker asks God to answer him and enlighten his eyes so that he will not fall into the sleep of death. He asks that his enemy and foes not be allowed to rejoice in his defeat and downfall.

paragraphs.paragraph: Despite his troubles and dangers, the speaker trusts in God's kindness, his only support. He hopes for salvation, his heart rejoices, and he promises to sing to God for the gift of salvation he has received.
paragraphs.title: Trust in Kindness and Joy in Salvation

easy.explanation: He says, “I have trusted in thy mercy.”
easy.q: In what does the speaker trust?

easy.explanation: The speaker says, “my heart shall rejoice in thy salvation.”
He declares, “I will sing unto the LORD.”
easy.q: What will the speaker do unto the LORD?

answers: Trust in God's mercy and salvation
medium.explanation: The speaker trusts in God's mercy and rejoices in His salvation.
medium.q: What enables the speaker to move from distress toward joy?

medium.explanation: The speaker first trusts, then rejoices, and finally promises to sing.
medium.q: What is the order of ideas in verse 6?

medium.explanation: To deal bountifully is to show abundant goodness or kindness.
medium.q: What does “he hath dealt bountifully with me” mean?

answers: From sorrow and abandonment to trust and joy
From a heading to an author's name
challenge.explanation: The earlier verses describe distress, while verse 6 expresses confidence and rejoicing.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between verses 2–3 and verse 6?

answers: It is the foundation of his trust
It is the enemy overcoming him
It causes the sleep of death
challenge.explanation: The speaker says that he has trusted in God's mercy.
challenge.q: What role does God's mercy play for the speaker?

answers: He responds with gratitude and worship
He wants his enemy to triumph
challenge.explanation: His song expresses gratitude for God's abundant goodness and salvation.
challenge.q: What does the promise to sing reveal about the speaker's final attitude?

paragraphs.idea: Despite his troubles and dangers, the speaker trusts in God's kindness, his only support. He hopes for salvation, his heart rejoices, and he promises to sing to God for the gift of salvation he has received.
